content: 1. Hyoscyamine spray and glucagon: Co-administration of glucagon and hyoscyamine spray increases the risk of gastrointestinal toxicity due to additive effects on the inhibition of gastrointestinal motility. This interaction may lead to adverse gastrointestinal reactions. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. 2. Hyoscyamine spray and glycopyrronium tosylate (topical): The concurrent use of hyoscyamine spray and glycopyrronium tosylate may result in additive anticholinergic adverse effects due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 3. Hyoscyamine spray and pramlintide: The combination of hyoscyamine spray and pramlintide is contraindicated due to synergistic inhibition of gastrointestinal motility, which can lead to severe adverse effects. 4. Hyoscyamine spray and revefenacin: Both drugs decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Co-administration may result in additive anticholinergic effects. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. Hyoscyamine spray and secretin: Hyoscyamine spray decreases the effects of secretin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Concomitant use may cause a hyporesponse to stimulation testing with secretin. Discontinue anticholinergic drugs at least five half-lives before administering secretin. 6. Hyoscyamine spray and sofpironium (topical): Co-administration of these agents may result in additive anticholinergic adverse effects due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 7. Hyoscyamine spray and umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol (inhaled): The combination of these drugs may increase the toxicity of either agent due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Hyoscyamine spray and abobotulinumtoxinA: Hyoscyamine spray may potentiate the effects of abobotulinumtoxinA, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Hyoscyamine spray and aclidinium: Both drugs decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor for additive anticholinergic effects. 10. Hyoscyamine spray and amantadine: Co-administration may enhance central nervous system (CNS) side effects due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Hyoscyamine spray and amitriptyline: Both drugs decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor for potential additive effects. 12. Hyoscyamine spray and amoxapine: Co-administration may result in additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Hyoscyamine spray and anticholinergic/sedative combinations: Concurrent use may lead to additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions. 14. Hyoscyamine spray and aripiprazole: Aripiprazole increases the effects of hyoscyamine spray through pharmacodynamic synergism. Additionally, hyoscyamine spray may decrease the levels of aripiprazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Hyoscyamine spray and atracurium: Both drugs decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor for potential additive effects. 16. Hyoscyamine spray and atropine: Co-administration may result in additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Hyoscyamine spray and belladonna alkaloids: Both agents decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor for potential additive effects. 18. Hyoscyamine spray and benperidol: Benperidol increases the effects of hyoscyamine spray through pharmacodynamic synergism. Additionally, hyoscyamine spray may decrease the levels of benperidol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Hyoscyamine spray and benztropine: Both drugs decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor for potential additive effects. 20. Hyoscyamine spray and bethanechol: Bethanechol increases cholinergic effects, while hyoscyamine spray decreases them. The overall effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor closely.
